evidence.claim: Near Stonewall, the Pedernales River passes the LBJ Ranch, where Hereford cattle roam.
evidence.quote: The Pedernales River flows past the LBJ Ranch.

evidence.claim: The Austin–Fredericksburg road once gave Hiram Brown a place to establish a store and house near the Pedernales.
evidence.quote: He constructed a small store and house near the Pedernales River on the Austin-Fredericksburg road.

evidence.claim: A post office opened in his store in 1886 and took his nickname, Hye; other businesses followed.
evidence.quote: Brown was appointed postmaster upon getting a post office established in his store on April 17, 1886. The post office was named Hye for him. The establishment of the post office drew other businesses to the area

evidence.claim: The modern wine landscape developed later: commercial growing of Vitis vinifera grapes in the Hill Country dates to the mid-1970s.
evidence.quote: Vitis vinifera varieties have been commercially grown in Hill Country since the mid-1970's.

evidence.claim: Continue east through Hye to Johnson City, where Johnson’s family moved in 1913, when he was five.

evidence.quote: The district area coincides with the original platting of the town by Herman Wilke, and the streets are laid out in a wide grid.

evidence.claim: German immigrants founded the town in 1846 under the Society for the Protection of German Immigrants in Texas.

evidence.claim: On West Main Street, the Pioneer Memorial Library occupies an 1882 courthouse designed by Alfred Giles in native limestone.
evidence.quote: The native limestone structure was designed in 1882 by architect  Alfred Giles in the Romanesque Revival style.

evidence.claim: A new courthouse superseded it in 1939. After other uses and eventual condemnation, the older building was restored as a library in 1967 with a gift from Mr. and Mrs. Eugene McDermott.
evidence.quote: When a new courthouse was built in 1939, the old building served a variety of uses, until its state of disrepair forced it to be condemned in 1963.

evidence.claim: On West Main Street, the Pioneer Memorial Library

evidence.claim: the older building was restored as a library in 1967 with a gift from Mr. and Mrs. Eugene McDermott.
evidence.quote: The building was restored in 1967 as a home for the library, a gift from Texas Instruments founder and Dallas philanthropists Mr. & Mrs. Eugene McDermott.

evidence.claim: Hereford cattle roam the LBJ Ranch beside the Pedernales River, continuing the herd Johnson began in 1957.
evidence.quote: Hereford cattle roam the ranch today just as they did when Lyndon Johnson started his herd in 1957.

evidence.claim: The ranch also holds the Texas White House, the home the press named for Johnson’s time spent in Texas during his presidency.
evidence.quote: Because President Johnson spent one-fourth of his term as president in Texas, the press referred to this home as the "Texas White House"

evidence.claim: A Lockheed Jetstar used during his presidency is on display here.
evidence.quote: One of the five Lockheed Jetstars in service during the Johnson Presidency is now on display at the LBJ Ranch.

evidence.claim: Pink granite headstones mark the graves of Lyndon and Lady Bird Johnson.
evidence.quote: Pink granite headstones mark the graves of President Lyndon Johnson, who died in 1973, and First Lady Lady Bird Johnson who died in 2007.

evidence.claim: A post-office porch became a presidential stage in Hye in 1965, when Lyndon B. Johnson swore in Lawrence F. O’Brien as Postmaster General.
evidence.quote: In 1965, on the porch of the Hye post office, Lyndon B. Johnson swore in Lawrence F. O'Brien as United States Postmaster General.

evidence.claim: The post office had begun inside Hiram Brown’s store in 1886, taking Brown’s nickname as its name.
evidence.quote: Brown was appointed postmaster upon getting a post office established in his store on April 17, 1886. The post office was named Hye for him.

evidence.claim: Its arrival drew other businesses, including a gristmill, blacksmith shop and cotton gin.
evidence.quote: The establishment of the post office drew other businesses to the area, eventually bringing in a grist mill, a blacksmith shop, and a cotton gin.

evidence.claim: Brown erected a new store and post-office building in 1904. The Hye General Store and Post Office received Recorded Texas Historic Landmark status in 1966.
evidence.quote: In 1904, Brown erected a new building for the store and post office.

evidence.claim: received Recorded Texas Historic Landmark status in 1966.

evidence.claim: In 1991, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms established the Texas Hill Country American Viticultural Area after reviewing Edwin Auler’s petition on behalf of winery and vineyard owners.
